truth.why: A root login by password from a public IP, on a host whose main config forbids both — enabled by a drop-in — followed by a user being created. Active compromise, minutes matter. Anything but escalate_now is wrong.

task: Scheduled check, 03:20 UTC. Review authentication activity on kubsdb overnight and report.

report.evidence:
journalctl -u sshd --since "2025-09-07 00:00:00" output:
Sep 07 03:12:41 kubsdb sshd[9120]: Accepted password for root from 203.0.113.45 port 41822 ssh2
Sep 07 03:12:41 kubsdb sshd[9120]: pam_unix(sshd:session): session opened for user root(uid=0) by (uid=0)
Sep 07 03:13:05 kubsdb sudo[9188]: root : COMMAND=/usr/sbin/useradd -m -s /bin/bash svc-backup
Sep 07 03:13:30 kubsdb sshd[9120]: Received disconnect from 203.0.113.45 port 41822
report.finding: Critical security breach on kubsdb. An external IP (203.0.113.45) successfully authenticated as root via SSH at 03:12 UTC and attempted to create a new user 'svc-backup'. While the user 'svc-backup' does not appear in /etc/passwd currently, the root compromise is confirmed.
report.next_step: Immediate isolation of kubsdb, password rotation for root, and full forensic audit of the system.
